messages.content: Find a grocery store near me with organic fruits and vegetables in Houston.

function.name: grocery_store_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby grocery stores based on specific criteria like organic fruits and vegetables. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Houston, TX

categories.description: Categories of items to be found in the grocery store. Default is all if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to find a grocery store near them (in Houston) that has organic fruits and vegetables. We have a tool `grocery_store_find_nearby` which takes location and categories. We'll call it.

We need to pass location as "Houston, TX". For categories we want both Organic Fruits and Vegetables? But the schema says categories can be one or more from list: "Organic", "Vegetables", "Fruits", etc. It doesn't allow specifying subcategory like "organic fruit"? Actually categories includes "Organic" category; maybe they mean organic produce overall. So we could set categories=["Organic","Vegetables"]? Wait categories type is union of strings OR array? Let's read carefully:

```
categories?: "Organic" | "Vegetables" | "Fruits" | "Dairy" | "Seafood" | "Bakery"[]
```

It seems ambiguous but likely means optional parameter categories may be either single string among those options or an array of such strings. In our case we might specify ["Organic","Vegetables"]. That should work.

We'll use the function.
